one_line: Sangam-era Tamil poet of the hill-country courts, famed in tradition as bard and companion of Vel Pari.

appearance.age_look: Late 30s, lean and wiry build, slightly weathered but energetic.
appearance.face: Oval face with high cheekbones, medium-brown complexion, sharp nose, thin lips, faint stubble shadow, a small vertical tilak-like sandal mark on the forehead; default expression is calm, observant and slightly intense, with a hint of melancholy.
appearance.hair: Thick wavy black hair pulled back into a mid-length low knot at the nape, a few loose strands framing the temples; simple narrow cloth headband in muted maroon tied around the head, knot at the back.
appearance.costume: Era-appropriate Tamil bardic attire: a knee-length off-white cotton angavastram-style wrap tunic with short sleeves and a modest round neck, worn over a tightly wrapped reddish-brown cotton veshti/dhoti falling to the ankles with a narrow darker border; a dull green cotton shawl draped from the left shoulder across the torso and back for modesty; simple leather sandals; minimal jewellery—a single small copper ear ring in the left ear and a thin beaded wrist-thread—textiles plain but slightly crinkled, suggesting travel.
appearance.signature: A palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with a dark cord and tucked under his right arm, with a slender wooden stylus held lightly in his right hand as if ready to compose.

ref_desc: Kapilar is a late-30s lean Tamil poet with medium-brown skin, wavy black hair in a low knot and maroon headband, wearing an off-white tunic, reddish-brown veshti, dull green shawl, simple jewellery, and carrying a palm-leaf manuscript bundle with wooden stylus in earth-toned colours.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Kapilar: a late-30s lean Tamil poet with medium-brown complexion, oval face, high cheekbones, sharp nose, faint stubble shadow and calm, slightly intense eyes, marked by a small vertical sandal mark on his forehead. His thick wavy black hair is pulled into a mid-length low knot at the nape, with a few loose strands at the temples, wrapped by a narrow muted maroon cloth headband tied at the back. Dress him in historically plausible early Tamil bardic attire: a modest off-white cotton wrap tunic with short sleeves and round neck reaching to mid-thigh, over a tightly wrapped ankle-length reddish-brown cotton veshti/dhoti with a darker narrow border, and a dull green cotton shawl draped from his left shoulder diagonally across his torso and back, ensuring his chest and legs are fully covered and family-safe. Add simple leather sandals, a single small copper earring in his left ear, and a thin beaded thread bracelet on his right wrist; textiles should look plain, slightly crinkled and travel-worn. Place a tied palm-leaf manuscript bundle under his right arm, and a slender wooden stylus lightly held in his right hand as his signature prop. Use a grounded earth-tone palette of off-white, reddish-brown, muted maroon, dull green and dark brown, and show him from multiple angles while keeping the same face, hair, clothing and props consistent.
